faqs.q: When can bats be excluded from a Hialeah home?
faqs.a: Bat exclusion is legal in Florida from August 15 through April 15. Excluding or blocking bats during maternity season, April 16 through August 14, is illegal under FWC Rule 68A-9.010. The house bats here are Brazilian free-tailed and evening bats. In maternity season our crew can inspect, identify the roost, and schedule the exclusion for the legal window — and a bat found in a room with a sleeping person is a county health department call first.

faqs.q: We think we saw a python near our Homestead grove — what should we do?
faqs.a: Do not approach it, photograph from a safe distance if you can, note the exact location, and report it to FWC's exotic species reporting channels. Burmese pythons are Prohibited species managed through FWC's programs — the Python Action Team and permitted removal efforts; on private land they may be humanely killed with landowner permission, and they must be killed on site, never transported alive. Private wildlife companies do not sell python removal as a service, and anyone who offers to catch one live and take it away is describing an illegal transport.
